abstract: Brain pericytes arise from two embryonic lineages, neural crest and mesoderm, but it is unknown whether these origins produce molecularly distinct pericyte populations. Using zebrafish lineage-tracing transgenics, we mapped neural crest- and mesoderm-derived pericytes across the brain from larval to adult stages. Neural crest-derived pericytes occupied the forebrain and mesoderm-derived pericytes occupied the midbrain and hindbrain at early stages. A population of neural crest-derived pericytes then appeared in the dorsal midbrain by 10 days post-fertilization and persisted into adulthood. A small population of mesoderm-derived pericytes also appeared in the ventral forebrain of juvenile and adult fish. Bulk RNA sequencing of FACS-isolated adult pericytes showed that the two lineages share expression of canonical pericyte genes, with only 30 genes differentially expressed. Fluorescent in situ hybridization validated one neural crest-enriched gene, plpp3, and several mesoderm-enriched genes, including loxl2b. Together, these data suggest that despite distinct embryonic origins and regional bias, brain pericyte lineages converge on a largely shared molecular profile.
